paper.title_en: Advancing Quantum Reinforcement Learning with Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search and Adaptive Non-local Observables
paper.abstract_en: Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) using variational quantum circuits (VQCs) is constrained by fixed measurement protocols and hand-designed circuit ansätze. Adaptive Non-local Observables (ANO) and Differentiable Quantum Architecture Search (DiffQAS) address these issues independently, but to our knowledge have not been combined or compared in a single QRL framework. We present an ablation of ANO and DiffQAS within the Quantum Time-series Transformer (QTSTransformer), evaluated on a 2 x 2 factorial design across six environments--two classic-control tasks and four Atari 2600 games. Three findings emerge. First, the quantum agent outperforms a matched classical transformer baseline on five of six environments, with absolute scores ranging from 360.0 vs 304.0 (MarioBros) to 17.2 vs 2.5 (Breakout), while using approximately 12.5x fewer transformer parameters on the four Atari environments (more modestly so on the two classic-control tasks). Second, ANO and DiffQAS provide complementary benefits: ANO yields the largest gain on continuous-state CartPole (347.7 vs 223.2), while DiffQAS yields the largest absolute Atari gains (Breakout 17.2 vs 3.0; DonkeyKong 70.0 vs 37.0). Third, combining both innovations exhibits an asymmetric interaction: ANO-dominant tasks tolerate DiffQAS, whereas DiffQAS-dominant tasks degrade when ANO is added. These results provide design guidance for QRL agents: select between ANO and DiffQAS according to whether the bottleneck is the measurement basis or the gate topology, rather than applying both indiscriminately.
